title: Rubix: Reducing the Overhead of Secure Rowhammer Mitigations via Randomized Line-to-Row Mapping
problem: Complex Rowhammer attacks like Half-Double break traditional victim-refresh mitigations, and while aggressor-based schemes (AQUA, SRS, Blockhammer) provide security, they incur prohibitive slowdowns (15%-600%) at low thresholds expected in the near future.
motivation: Deploying practical Rowhammer mitigations at low thresholds is essential for securing modern memory systems against evolving attacks.
method: Rubix uses randomized line-to-row mapping to reduce the overhead of secure Rowhammer mitigations by spreading cache line accesses across physical rows, making it harder for attackers to concentrate accesses on a single aggressor row. The technique works with existing mitigation schemes like row-migration and access-control to reduce their performance overhead while maintaining security against sophisticated attacks.
key_novelty: Randomized line-to-row mapping as a lightweight technique to reduce the performance overhead of existing Rowhammer mitigation schemes.
contributions: Identifies prohibitive overhead problems in existing aggressor-based Rowhammer mitigations at low thresholds
Proposes randomized line-to-row mapping mechanism to reduce mitigation overhead
Demonstrates practical performance improvements while maintaining security against Half-Double and other attacks
Provides evaluation at various Rowhammer thresholds to guide future mitigation deployment

metrics.speedup: Reduction in slowdown compared to AQUA, SRS, and Blockhammer at low thresholds
metrics.other: Performance overhead percentage relative to unprotected baseline

limitations: Limitations not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Rowhammer mitigation via randomized memory mapping
